name: The Ginkgo of the Bolwerken

location.address: De Bolwerken, on the lawn between the Noorderbrug and the Kruisweg crossing, Haarlem

verified_sources: https://www.ivn.nl/app/uploads/sites/23/2024/06/Boekje-Mon-bomen_Haarlem_spreads_DIGI.pdf (IVN/Bomenstichting monumental-trees walking guide for Haarlem; register nr 1696661 appears in the guide's own text, cross-confirming the register entry as an independently-selected stop on its Bolwerken walk)
access: Free, open park at any time
transport: 10-12 minute walk from Haarlem Centraal station
verify_notes: Register (netherlands-lrmb nr 1696661): planted 1910-1920, standing alone on a lawn at the foot of a slope in De Bolwerken, the park JD Zocher laid out from 1828 on Haarlem's demolished fortifications. Register history note (translated): 'the ginkgo is from almost a hundred years later [than the park's 1828 design] and stands on a lawn at the foot of a hill.' owner_category gemeente, visitable ja, visible ja, status 3 (=alive/standing in the register's own status coding, consistent with the other Kenaupark register entries already published as haa_007/008/009 which share this status value). Second source: the tree's register number (1696661) appears verbatim in the IVN/Bomenstichting 'Langs monumentale bomen in Haarlem' walking-guide PDF, which independently selected it as a stop on the Bolwerken route -- this PDF is a text/graphics-only file I could not fully OCR/extract in this session (no pdftotext or PDF library available), so I am citing only the confirmed cross-reference (matching register ID present in the guide's text stream), not any prose or measurement from it. A WebSearch AI summary of the same PDF offered extra descriptive text about ginkgos generally; per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule I have not carried any of its specific figures into this record. Flagged only because the second-source confirmation is a number-match rather than a read sentence; nothing here casts doubt on the tree's identity or standing. No news of removal found. location_precision approximate per brief default: register gives a specific descriptive point (park-layout description) but I have no independent photo/imagery confirmation of the exact trunk position.

name: The Oak Pair of Statenbolwerk
species: Oak (Quercus robur or Quercus petraea; the register does not specify which)

location.address: Statenbolwerk, west side, at the start of the footpath, Haarlem

verified_sources: https://www.ivn.nl/app/uploads/sites/23/2024/06/Boekje-Mon-bomen_Haarlem_spreads_DIGI.pdf (register nr 1696664 appears in the guide's text, an independent selection of the same pair as a walk stop)
access: Free, open park at any time
transport: 10-12 minute walk from Haarlem Centraal station
verify_notes: Register (netherlands-lrmb nr 1696664): two oaks ('Eikenduo'), planted 1850-1860, n_trees 2, marking the entrance to the walking area at the west side of Statenbolwerk. Register history (translated): 'From 1828 the bolwerken are a green walking area, designed by JD Zocher. Villa building in the area dates from 1860. These oaks were planted then too... The trees mark the entrance to the walking area.' owner_category gemeente, visitable ja, visible ja, status 3. This is a compact two-tree ensemble at one obvious spot (a path entrance), passing the collectible-point test the same way Kenaupark's already-published plane group and bald cypress group do. Species: the register calls it only 'eik' (oak) without naming pedunculate vs sessile; I could not find a second source specifying which, so per the 'if you don't know, publish it and ask the reader' rule the species field states the ambiguity rather than guessing. Second source: register number 1696664 independently appears in the IVN/Bomenstichting Haarlem monumental-trees walking guide (same PDF-ID-matching caveat as haa_010: confirmed by ID match in the extracted text stream, not by reading full prose, since the guide's text layer would not OCR cleanly this session). No death/felling signal found for this specific pair in my searches (distinct from the confirmed-dead beech at Statenbolwerk nr 2, see blocked list).

name: The Caucasian Wingnut of Statenbolwerk
verified_sources: https://www.ivn.nl/app/uploads/sites/23/2024/06/Boekje-Mon-bomen_Haarlem_spreads_DIGI.pdf (register nr 1686176 appears in the guide's text)
access: Visible from the public Statenbolwerk footpath; the tree stands within the grounds of Staten Bolwerk 1, a private villa (owner_category 'particulier' in the register), so the trunk itself is not something a visitor can walk up to. The register itself marks it visitable/visible ('ja'/'ja').
transport: 10-12 minute walk from Haarlem Centraal station
verify_notes: Register (netherlands-lrmb nr 1686176): Caucasian wingnut, planted 1900-1910, at Statenbolwerk 1, a villa dating from 1860 in the Zocher-designed Bolwerken park. Register history (translated): 'The bolwerken have been laid out from 1832, first by JD Zocher and later also by his son LP Zocher. The villas date from 1860 and later. The wingnut dates from the beginning of the 20th century.' owner_category is 'particulier' (private) but the register's own visitable/visible fields both say 'ja', which is why this is delivered rather than blocked -- treated per hard rule 10's view-only test: genuinely visible from public ground, pin should mark the viewing place rather than claim trunk access, and access says plainly what a visitor will and won't get. Flagging because I have not independently confirmed how much of the tree is actually visible from the path versus screened by the villa's own garden; a future pass with street-level imagery should tighten this. Second source: register number 1686176 appears in the IVN/Bomenstichting walking guide's text stream (ID-match only, same caveat as the other two Bolwerken entries -- the PDF's prose did not extract cleanly this session). No death signal found.

name: The Beech Ensemble of Statenbolwerk

location.address: Statenbolwerk, along the path near number 26, Haarlem

verified_sources: https://www.ivn.nl/app/uploads/sites/23/2024/06/Boekje-Mon-bomen_Haarlem_spreads_DIGI.pdf (register nr 1696662 appears in the guide's text)
access: Free, open park at any time
transport: 10-12 minute walk from Haarlem Centraal station
verify_notes: Register (netherlands-lrmb nr 1696662): four beeches ('Beukenensemble'), planted 1850-1860, n_trees 4, along a path beside Statenbolwerk near number 26. Register history (translated): 'The bolwerken are the old defensive works of Haarlem. In 1828 JD Zocher was commissioned to make a green walking park here... winding paths run over the heights and along the water. The railway was built in 1835 and led to further building on the south side of the bolwerken. The seed of this beech group is dated to the mid-19th century.' owner_category gemeente, visitable ja, visible ja, status 3. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION FROM A KNOWN-DEAD TREE: a separate, single copper/red beech ('rode beuk'/'bruine beuk', Fagus sylvatica purpurea, register nr 1690404) at Statenbolwerk nr 2, roughly 200m from this ensemble's location at nr 26, blew down in storm Eunice on 18-24 February 2022 (sources: boomzorg.nl and haarlem105.nl both report a 222-year-old red beech felled by the storm near Kloppersingel/Staten Bolwerk, wood since made into cutting boards and knives). This ensemble is a different register entry (different nr, different address point, ordinary green Fagus sylvatica per the register rather than the purpurea/copper cultivar, and a 4-tree group rather than a lone specimen), so I am delivering it, but flagging clearly given the location overlap and beech-on-beech risk of confusion, and I have NOT delivered the separately-listed 'Groene beuk Bolwerken' (nr 1690403, a single green beech at Statenbolwerk nr 14, also possibly ~200 years old per the register's own text) because I could not rule out overlap/confusion with the fallen tree to my own satisfaction in this session; it is recorded as a lead instead. Second source for this ensemble: register number 1696662 appears in the IVN/Bomenstichting walking guide's text stream (ID-match only, prose not extracted -- do not carry over the WebSearch AI summary's specific height/circumference figures for this tree, they were not verified against the actual page and are excluded per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule).
